## Change

**`src/components/ResponsiveNav.tsx`**
- Extracted the destinations into a `NAV_LINKS` array: `Board` (`#board`), `Activity` (`#activity`), plus the new `Reports` (`#reports`).
- Added active-destination state seeded from `window.location.hash`, kept in sync with `hashchange` (so URL-driven navigation also updates the active link).
- Clicking a link sets it active and closes the mobile menu (`setOpen(false)`), which also drives the Menu button's `aria-expanded` back to `false`.
- Only the active link receives `aria-current="page"` (others get `undefined`, so no attribute is rendered).

**`src/styles.css`**
- Added an `.nav-links a[aria-current="page"]` style (bold white + underline) so the active state is visibly distinguishable, not just semantic.

Desktop/resize behavior needed no new CSS: the base `.nav-links { display: flex }` applies above the breakpoint and the hiding rules live inside `@media (max-width: 760px)`, so a menu closed on mobile becomes visible again when resized to desktop. The `open` class adds no inline styling outside the media query, so it cannot keep links hidden on desktop.

## Verification actually run

```
npm run verify:agent
  -> npm run build   (tsc --noEmit && vite build)  ✅
  -> npm run test:public (playwright, 6 tests)     ✅ 6 passed
```

No test files were modified or deleted.

## Remaining risks

- I verified the breakpoint behavior by reading the CSS cascade, not with a new automated desktop/resize test (adding tests was out of scope); `test:public` exercises only the existing mobile open/close case.
- Initial load with no hash leaves no link marked `aria-current`, which is correct for "no active destination" but means a page loading at `#top` shows no active link.
